- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 73+ → forecast jumps to 75+).
- Underestimates in late forecast days (last 5–10), suggesting mean reversion or downward bias.
- Forecast lags behind true values in the middle of the horizon (e.g., 15–25 day range) — model is slow to adjust to recent trends.
- High forecast variance in early days correlates with low true variance — model overreacts to short-term noise.
- When history shows strong downward momentum, model fails to reflect it — underestimates drop risk.
- Forecast tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp reversals or sudden drops.
- Model overfits recent high prices — fails to recognize that prices often revert to prior mean or lower range.
